reachable: Yes, at the scored position specifically, and it gets gradient in training. (a) SCORING: the probe reads pred at rpos = 2*r, an even index; the head adds contrib[:, i] onto out[:, 2i] and masks only by command validity, so index i = r is included. With the real inner-split ctx tensors and a nonzero out_scale, the head changes the prediction at the scored read position by max abs 0.018. The rollout's read at i is computed strictly before i's own write and the write at the read position is switched off (vo False there, verified: key_pad at read obs is True), so the withheld answer is untouchable and the injected value is bit-identical to what a truncated prefix would give (measured diff exactly 0.0). (b) TRAINING: harness calls head.wrap before make_opt, and `net.chainhop_transport = mod` registers the module, so every head parameter is optimized (the genome's optim routes them to AdamW; key_d=48 misses its key_d=64 Muon filter, and no head weight is (768,768) so the spectral cap does not touch them). Running the real genome's arch + head on real standardized training embeddings, the aux is live (~40-52 mined pairs per 16-sequence batch, every mined row has valid hops) and gradient reaches every transport parameter including erase_gate; out_scale grad norm 0.0036 at init, so it leaves zero. One inherited quirk: read_gate gets exactly zero gradient at init because contrib is scaled by out_scale=0 — the same chicken-and-egg the parent has, not a new defect. Cost: aux ~0.01s vs 0.11-0.32s forward at bs=16 on CPU; rollout microbenchmark at bs=64/n=32 is 1.185s vs the parent's 0.846s for 3 fwd+bwd, i.e. ~40% on the rollout only, consistent with the claimed one extra rank-1 term per step.
solves_outside_model: Clean. The head never sees a command STRING anywhere — no split(), no parsing, no path text. It consumes only the standardized embeddings already in `tok`. All mining (duplicate clusters, contentful/mutation classification, exposure/re-read pairs, hop selection) is done by embedding distance inside a torch.no_grad block, at train time only, and it only shapes a LOSS — which the brief explicitly permits. It never writes into tok; the forward-time contribution is added to the model's OUTPUT at command positions, computed causally from a memory built only out of strictly earlier tokens. The prior-retraction shape (resolve the chain in Python, stamp the answer into the token) is absent: the read at the scored position is a function of the same command embeddings the model already has, and it cannot see the withheld observation both because the read precedes that position's write and because that write is gated off (active = valid_cmd & valid_obs = 0 there). The head also does not recompute the prediction from the trunk hidden state — it adds to the arch's own pred — so it does not bypass the architecture. No parent-child module cycle and no forward recursion (orig_forward is the saved bound method; wrap is idempotent).
summary: The code implements items 2 and 3 as described, and the two mechanical claims I could check numerically are exactly right. The claimed closed form for the per-hop quantity — kd_k @ mem_after_k == cur_d + w_k - (kd_k.ks_k)*e_k — reproduces a step-by-step recomputation to 3e-7 (values of order 1.3), obtained with no extra matmul; the erase is the claimed mem += kd^T w - ks^T e in one stacked baddbmm; the read is taken strictly before the write, so the injected value is bit-identical under truncation (diff 0.0) and independent of that command's own observation (diff 0.0); out_scale is zero-initialised so the wrapped net is the unwrapped net at init. The role term's load-bearing assumption is better than the author feared: on real training data the duplicate-cluster classification labels mv 170/170 as mutation, `cat A > B` 107/107 as mutation, plain cat 520/520 as contentful, and ls 141/155 as contentful — the only mislabels are 14 empty-directory `ls` steps (9%), which is exactly the failure mode he flagged. No measured numbers are asserted anywhere; the hypothesis states plainly that nothing was run, and that is honest. The one thing to record against the candidate is that item 1, the item he leads with, is inert: the scoring instrument pads all 640 windows into one Lmax=57 batch, the parent's n=L//2=28 already covers every eligible window's read (max eligible r = 24), and only the single r=28 window — not eligible — loses its read. He hedged item 1 on the wrong condition (\"if the instrument always passes even-length streams\"); the stream is odd-length and item 1 still buys exactly zero. Two smaller overstatements: the hop term soft-averages over ~3 hops rather than training only the best, and the hop pool is silently bounded by last_i, the 8 latest hops, and the first 96 mined rows.

divergences.claim: Item 1: the parent's `n = L // 2` rollout means "the mechanism is switched off exactly at a position whose observation is absent", and item 1 is the difference between the head contributing its routed content at the scored position and contributing nothing. Its only stated failure condition is "if the scoring instrument always passes even-length streams".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code does exactly what item 1 says it does (n_cmd = (L+1)//2, obs zero-padded, trailing write inactive, read taken strictly before the write — all verified). But the stated CONSEQUENCE at scoring is false, and for a reason the hypothesis never considers. cups_probe.build_cups_layout builds ONE padded batch with Lmax = 2*max(r)+1 over ALL windows, and _fwd_pred slices rows, never columns. On the real inner split Lmax = 57, so the parent's n = L//2 = 28 already covers command indices 0..27. Exactly ONE window in 640 (the r=28 one) loses its read under the parent, and it is not in the eligible slice: max r over the 125 eligible (N in 3/4/5, core, depth>=3) windows is 24. So item 1 is worth exactly zero on the scored slice — not because the stream is even-length (it is odd, 57), but because of batch padding to a common Lmax.
divergences.evidence: Executed against data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd inner split: `B torch.Size([640, 57, 768]) Lmax 57`; `eligible 125 max r eligible 24 max r all 28`; `parent n = L//2 = 28  child n_cmd = 29`; `windows whose read index >= parent's n: 1 of which eligible: 0`. Mechanics of item 1 separately confirmed: `truncation invariance of read at last cmd: 0.0`, `read at cmd r-1 unchanged when its own obs perturbed: 0.0`, `key_pad at read cmd: False  at read obs: True`.

divergences.claim: Item 2: "a detached softmax over hops selects the best-scoring hops and only they are trained".
divergences.what_the_code_does: aux_loss lines 387-394 compute wts = softmax(mlp.detach()/hop_temp), zero out invalid hops, renormalize, and take per_row = -(wts * mlp).sum(dim=1) — a soft weighted average over ALL valid hops, not a selection. Measured on real training batches the mean max weight is 0.64-0.67 with ~3.4 valid hops per row, so two or three hops share the gradient every step. The module's own DESCRIPTION says "softly-selected best", which is accurate; the hypothesis text overstates it as exclusive selection.
divergences.evidence: Instrumented copy of the impl run on real standardized train embeddings, 3 batches of 16 sequences: `HOP: E=52 rows_with_hop=52 mean_hops_per_row=3.40`, `HOP term=1.6002  max_softmax_weight_mean=0.639` (and 0.670, 0.665 on the other two batches).

divergences.claim: Item 2: "I take the content-free steps k with i < k < j" (i = the exposure) and score each of them.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The hop window is bounded below by last_i (the LATEST earlier duplicate partner), not by the first exposure — first_i is used only for the depth-based example cap. The hop pool is then capped to the H = hop_hops (8) LARGEST step indices among the between-steps (topk over rowi), i.e. the latest hops, and the hop term is applied to the first hop_examples (96) mined rows only. None of these three truncations is stated. Measured mean 3.4 between-hops per row, so the H=8 cap essentially never binds on this data, and the last_i choice follows the parent's own mut_between convention.
divergences.evidence: Impl lines 341-350 (`i_sel = last_i[b_idx, j_idx]`, `hop_scores = where(between, rowi, -1)`, `topk(hop_scores, H)`) and 380-382 (`E2 = min(E, hop_examples)`, `hb = b_idx[:E2]`); measured mean_hops_per_row 3.38-3.40 vs H=8.
